newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil cargoes steady, barges dormant.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil cargoes steady, barges dormant.

text.p: European gas oil cargoes traded at steady levels on Thursday while barges saw lacklustre activity depressed by the high dollar, traders said.
August IPE settled 25 cents firmer at $165.25 a tonne after trading in a narrow range without much direction.

A 10,000 tonne cargo of 0.2 percent heating oil moved at August IPE $1.25, around unchanged, for the first half of August delivery. The product was talked slightly easier at around August IPE +$0.50/$1.00 later in the day.
A 20,000 tonne cargo of low sulphur diesel moved at September IPE +$4.50 for second half August delivery, down 75 cents from a flexi deal done on Wednesday.
First half August was talked at August IPE +$4.50/$4.75 with second half August talked at September IPE +$4.25/$4.50.
Barges remained lethargic, stalled by dollar strength. The dollar was higher at 1.8290 marks in late afternoon.
One trader reported moving a 1,000 tonne parcel of prompt Rotterdam refinery heating oil at August +$0.75, higher than the widely talked value of August IPE flat to 50 cents.
Traders predict barge activity will pick up when Iraqi oil exports resume and the oil complex comes under more pressure.
